# Toast

A short message that confirms an action and goes away.

**In Dense data.** Confirms a saved change. Family: feedback. Reference: Open UX (toast), MIT.

## See it live

[Open Toast in Storybook](http://localhost:6006/?path=/docs/components-toast--docs): every variant, the playground and its controls, in every theme.

## When to use it

- **Use it when:** Saved, sent, exported: something people should notice without stopping.
- **Not when:** A failure people must understand (alert or dialog), or a notice that stays (alert).

Instead:

- [Alert](./alert.md): Stays on the page.
- [Dialog](./dialog.md): Needs an answer.

## Variants

What each variant is for in any design system, and what Dense data decided, with the answers behind it.

| Axis | Variant | What it is for | In Dense data | Because |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tone | `neutral` | A plain confirmation. | A plain confirmation: Filters cleared. | <span title="How does it sound?">Terse</span> <small>(`voice.values`)</small> |
|  | `success` | Confirms that something people care about worked. | A short confirmation with the count: 12 alerts exported. | <span title="How does it sound?">Terse</span> <small>(`voice.values`)</small><br /><span title="How often do people repeat actions?">Constantly</span> <small>(`tasks.q2`)</small> |
|  | `danger` | Something failed in the background. | A background failure: name the record, then the fix. | <span title="How does it sound?">Terse</span> <small>(`voice.values`)</small><br /><span title="Where do the words matter most?">Errors and empty states</span> <small>(`voice.lands`)</small><br /><span title="What is a costly mistake?">Acting on the wrong record</span> <small>(`outcomes.q2`)</small> |

## How Dense data uses it

| Situation | Use | Not | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The words of an error | Name the record, then the fix. Flat and specific. | "Oops" or a vague apology | Experts act on the message; the record and the fix are all they need. Example: “Alert ALR-2042 not saved. Threshold must be between 0 and 100.” |
| A success message | A short confirmation with the count | Celebration | Confirm and get out of the way; the next task is waiting. Example: “12 alerts exported.” |

## Why it works this way

The answers that shaped Toast here. Change one, and the decisions above change with it.

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| How does it sound? (`voice.values`) | **Terse**. Experts want short labels and short messages. |
| How often do people repeat actions? (`tasks.q2`) | **Constantly**. The same actions repeat many times an hour. |
| Where do the words matter most? (`voice.lands`) | **Errors and empty states**. Errors and empty tables are where words decide the next action. |
| What is a costly mistake? (`outcomes.q2`) | **Acting on the wrong record**. Acting on the wrong row is the costly error. |

## What moves if an answer changes

For each answer above: the Toast decisions it would reopen, and the other answers that follow from it.

| If this changes | Toast decisions it reopens | Answers that follow |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `voice.values` | `tone/neutral`, `tone/success`, `tone/danger` | None |
| `tasks.q2` | `tone/success` | `outcomes.q1`, `scenarios.q2`, `color.count`, `motion.values`, `iconography.roles`, `iconography.lands`, `theming.values`, `voice.definition`, `components.definition`, `components.values`, `theming.count` |
| `voice.lands` | `tone/danger` | None |
| `outcomes.q2` | `tone/danger` | `color.lands`, `voice.lands` |

## Words

- Lead with the object, then the state: "Alert 2041 contained."
- Use numbers, not words for numbers.
- One verb per button. No "please", no exclamation marks.
- Use: Investigate, Filter, Assign, Escalated, Resolved. Avoid: Oops, Awesome, Please, Simply.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Cancel
- `content.action.destroy`: Delete
- `content.action.retry`: Retry
- `content.action.empty-action`: Change filters

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

Test before you ship:

- [ ] It is announced politely without taking focus, and stays long enough to read. undefined
- [ ] Nothing people must act on lives only in a toast. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add toast
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Component keys

The CSS variable is the key with `/` replaced by `-` and the base `@` dropped. Each key points to a token; values live only on primitives.

| Key | What it controls | Points to, light | Points to, dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `overlay/background` | Fill of a dialog, menu or toast. | `color.surface.raised` → `dense-data.theme.light.color.surface.raised` → `color.slate.light.0` | `color.surface.raised` → `dense-data.theme.dark.color.surface.raised` → `color.slate.dark.100` |
| `overlay/radius` | Corner radius of overlays. | `radius.container` → `dense-data.theme.base.radius.container` → `radius.4` | same |
| `overlay/shadow` | Shadow of overlays. | `elevation.overlay` → `dense-data.theme.light.elevation.overlay` → `shadow.overlay` | `elevation.overlay` → `dense-data.theme.dark.elevation.overlay` → `shadow.overlay-dark` |
| `overlay/scrim` | Color that dims the page behind a dialog. | `color.surface.scrim` → `dense-data.theme.light.color.surface.scrim` → `color.black.light.scrim` | `color.surface.scrim` → `dense-data.theme.dark.color.surface.scrim` → `color.black.dark.scrim` |
| `overlay/item-height` | Height of a menu item. | `size.control.default` → `size.32` | same |
| `tooltip/background` | Tooltip fill. | `color.surface.inverse` → `dense-data.theme.light.color.surface.inverse` → `color.slate.light.900` | `color.surface.inverse` → `dense-data.theme.dark.color.surface.inverse` → `color.slate.dark.900` |
| `tooltip/label` | Tooltip text. | `color.text.inverse` → `dense-data.theme.light.color.text.inverse` → `color.slate.light.0` | `color.text.inverse` → `dense-data.theme.dark.color.text.inverse` → `color.slate.dark.50` |
